_doc: Facts written once for a scope (#1610, knowledge slice C; design in docs/knowledge-model-design.md): what everyone in a village, on the north road, in a trade or a taught skill knows. Read by src/artificer/facts.ts (SCOPE_FACTS), behind the scope-facts rule switch. One plain line per fact. Every fact is true and names its source as `file § heading › label` (`file › label` for code), checked by facts-scope.test.ts; `canonised` dates facts written for the game to fit canon and then made canon by the owner (2026-10-11). Sensitivity is public and depth 1 unless set (elders reach 3 into their village; traders and the caravan master 3 into the road). For one topic in one scope, write the deeper fact first: a person answers with the first fact they know. People's and cultures' ways are not here: they're culture-lore.ts's (content/peoples-lore.json, content/cultures-lore.json). The road's generated regional facts (world/regional-facts.ts) come with slice F.

facts.text: The ford is older than the village; we only built where the river let us. This spring the grey took two more high fields, and the fences came down the hill again.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Above the village the high fields have gone grey-violet and hard

facts.text: Hollowford lives on barley and sheep: grain off the terraces, wool and hides off the folds. The ford brings the caravan, and the caravan buys.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Terraced barley on the last foothills, stone-walled sheepfolds

facts.text: Maren is our elder. Every spring after the flood she calls the whole village out to reset the ford stones, and then she counts them twice.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › mend the ford stones

facts.text: Tobin buys at the ford: hides, salt, a good knife, anything that travels well. He's quick with a price and fair with it.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › I buy what travels well

facts.text: Isa is our healer. She listens to a wound before she touches it, and she knows every green thing on the low slopes.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › she listens to a wound before she touches it

facts.text: Orrin keeps the forge, though he calls himself a woodwright. He's Bergfolk and hold-trained, whatever he tells you.
facts.source: src/artificer/answers.ts › hold-trained. You can hear it in how he sets an edge

facts.text: Hides off our folds are bought at the ford and carted down to Saltmere, where the salt keeps them.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › carry hides to Saltmere

facts.text: Hill-stone is the one thing we have plenty of: it walls the sheepfolds, and it makes the stepping stones across the ford.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › stone-walled sheepfolds, and a wide, shallow river crossed on a line of stepping stones

facts.text: Timber comes down from the copses above the terraces, and Orrin turns it into ploughs, gates and wheel spokes.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › skill: 'woodcraft'

facts.text: A goblin band lives in the old quarry above the ford. When the mill wheel cracked, they had it turning in a day and took barley for it.
facts.source: src/artificer/answers.ts › they had it turning in a day, and took barley for it

facts.text: The mere is lower every year, and the still water at the north end is creeping south. No birds drink there now, and the fish that wash up float belly-up.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › The north end of the mere has gone too still and faintly violet

facts.text: Saltmere lives on salt: raked off the white crust, packed into fish and pork, and carted up to the Gate. Fish and the sweet Pandor wells come after.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Salt for the caravan

facts.text: Gunnar is our elder. He was a [Watermaster] in the southern delta for forty years, and he still reads the mere every morning.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › in the southern delta for forty years

facts.text: Hedda trades here: salt fish, salt pork, salt everything. The caravan master still owes her three barrels, and she tells everyone.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › I owe Hedda three barrels

facts.text: Anselm teaches handcraft by the wells. He's Pandor: every sale and every winter goes into his book, and nobody argues with the book.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › nobody argues with the book

facts.text: Yrsa hunts the mere shore at dusk, when the birds come in. She's Viddfolk: few words, sharp eyes.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Few words, sharp eyes

facts.text: Liv is our healer, brisk and tireless. Her first word is always clean water, and everything else comes after.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Clean water first. Everything else after.

facts.text: Salt is raked off the crust at the edge of the mere and dried on racks. It goes up to the Gate by the cartload and comes back as coin, less the toll.
facts.source: src/artificer/answers.ts › Salt goes up to the Gate by the cartload

facts.text: Hides come down from Hollowford to be salted here, and Anselm sews the best of them into parkas and waterskins.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › 'hide-parka', 'waterskin'

facts.text: There isn't a tree on the steppe. Our hearths burn reed cut at the mere's edge, peat and dried dung, and what wood the carts bring is dear and goes to the smoke-racks.
facts.source: src/artificer/economy.ts › the hearths burn reed cut at the mere

facts.text: From Saltmere on, the Viddfolk keep the road. The Vidde Accords give them the route, and every nation signed.
facts.source: WORLD.md § Alliances and political arrangements › The Vidde Accords

facts.text: The iron price has doubled in forty winters, the Pandor book says, and the ore off the passes gets dearer every spring.
facts.source: src/artificer/answers.ts › the price has doubled in forty winters

facts.text: Iron is the Gate's trade, and the one thing cheaper inside the wall than out. The ore comes down off the passes.
facts.source: src/artificer/answers.ts › Iron is the one thing that

facts.text: The Gate lives on the toll and the market: everything going down to the lowlands is counted, taxed and sold here. Stone and iron come down off the pass.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Nothing goes into Mistheim

facts.text: From the Gate the road goes down the pass, and this winter the ash came down it thicker than ever. It settles grey on everything and won't brush off.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Ash comes down off the high pass on the west wind

facts.text: Veit is our elder. He counts the wagons, the heads and the goods, and he weighs every word as if it had a toll.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › he weighs every word as if it had a toll

facts.text: Sabine is the Gate's smith. Every hinge on the gate is hers, and the cart axles and the arrowheads too.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Gate hinges, cart axles, arrowheads

facts.text: Arvid trades inside the wall. He smiles, he's careful, and he's never the first to name a price.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › never the first to name a price

facts.text: Runa came down from the mountain holds to teach stonework. She's severe, then suddenly kind, the way the mountain is.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Severe, then suddenly kind

facts.text: The wall is pass stone, Steinfolk hands keep it mended, and the lowlands buy what's left over by the cartload.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › A stone wall across a narrow pass

facts.text: The Gate cuts its own wood on the slopes below the pass. The watch-fires and the forge burn most of it, and the trader buys what he can besides.
facts.source: src/artificer/economy.ts › Its fires and its forge burn wood cut on the slopes below the pass

facts.text: The Compact's people come through with stamped tokens instead of papers, and the wall lets them. The gate winch has needed a goblin more than once.
facts.source: src/artificer/answers.ts › come through with stamped tokens instead of papers

facts.text: Two places the caravan never camps: the still north end of the mere, and the pass below the Gate when the ash wind blows.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › No birds drink there

facts.text: The north road runs from the Reach to Mistheim: two days to Hollowford, two to Saltmere, two to Kestrel Gate, and two more to the lowlands.
facts.source: src/artificer/road.ts › { kind: 'travel', days: 2, to: 'Kestrel Gate' }

facts.text: Hollowford is the ford village, two days down from the Reach: barley, sheep and hides. The caravan crosses there before the spring flood, or waits a month.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › It is the only ford before the spring flood rises

facts.text: Saltmere is two days past the ford, on a long salt lake: salt for the caravan's meat, and the sweetest water on the road from the Pandor wells.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Salt for the caravan

facts.text: Kestrel Gate is the last wall before the lowlands. Everything going down pays its toll there and is counted.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › The caravan pays its toll and is counted here

facts.text: Lowland buyers pay silly money for tools made in the Reach, if they're sound. Sell your best past the Gate.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › In the lowlands they pay silly money for tools made in the Reach

facts.text: Mistheim's lowlands start two days past the Gate: river roads, inn smoke, and more people in one market square than in all three villages.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › more people in one market square than in all three villages together

facts.text: The road starts at the Reach's edge, where the caravan comes up each spring for whoever wintered there. Most years someone is waiting.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Most years someone is waiting

facts.text: Bodil is the caravan master. Twenty-two springs she's brought the wagons up the valley, and she's fond of every one like a relative.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Twenty-two springs

facts.text: Pim is the caravan's tinker, a goblin who talks to the axles. If it breaks between villages, it's his to fix.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › A goblin tinker who talks to the axles

facts.text: Ottilia is the caravan's herbwife: soft-spoken, older than anyone remembers, and quietly amused by everyone.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › soft-spoken, ancient, and quietly amused by everyone

facts.text: Runa is the caravan's route-singer. She keeps the accounts in songs and sells from her painted wagon on the travel days.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Viddfolk route-singer

facts.text: Tobin buys at Hollowford, Hedda at Saltmere and Arvid inside the Gate, and Runa sells from her painted wagon on the road between.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › she trades from her painted wagon on travel days

facts.text: Isa at Hollowford and Liv at Saltmere are healers, and Ottilia rides with the caravan. There's no healer at the Gate.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › p('hf-isa', 'Isa', 'healer'

facts.text: Orrin keeps a forge at Hollowford, but the real smithing is at the Gate, where Sabine works the iron.
facts.source: src/artificer/answers.ts › Real smithing wants iron and a reason to use it

facts.text: Anselm teaches at Saltmere and Runa at the Gate. Plenty of others will show you their craft if you ask.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › p('sm-anselm', 'Anselm', 'teacher'

facts.text: Each village has its elder: Maren at Hollowford, Gunnar at Saltmere, Veit at the Gate.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › p('sm-gunnar', 'Gunnar', 'elder'

facts.text: Yrsa at Saltmere is the road's hunter. She works the mere shore at dusk, when the birds come in.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › The mere birds come at dusk

facts.text: Nobody on the road has iron to sell but the Gate. The ore comes down off the passes, and Sabine there works it.
facts.source: src/artificer/answers.ts › Every pin I mend with is Gate iron

facts.text: Salt comes from Saltmere's mere, raked off the crust, and goes up to the Gate by the cartload.
facts.source: src/artificer/answers.ts › Salt goes up to the Gate by the cartload

facts.text: Hides come off Hollowford's folds and go down to Saltmere to be salted. Hedda there is owed hides by half the valley.
facts.source: src/artificer/answers.ts › owed hides by half the valley

facts.text: Every stretch of the north road is two days, and we sleep under an inn roof whenever we can: no one draws a blade there, and the cold stays out.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › roof no one draws a blade

facts.text: A caravan runs on sound axles, rested animals and an inn before dark. Lose any one of them and you lose a day.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › We stop at every inn we can reach before dark

facts.text: A healer listens first. Most of what ails a traveller is food, water or sleep gone missing, or a wound left dirty.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Most of what ails travellers is one of those three, missing

facts.text: For a wound: clean it, close it, keep it warm and dry. Most wounds that go bad were dirty before they were deep.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Clean water first. Everything else after.

facts.text: A trader's first rule: know what a thing is worth before anyone names a price, and let the other side name theirs first.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › never the first to name a price

facts.text: A hide's worth is in the scraping: a clean, dry hide fetches twice a greasy one, and salt keeps it sound on the road.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › I buy what travels well

facts.text: Hunting is mostly waiting: be where the animal will be before it is, and keep the wind in your face.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Patience gets you more than arrows

facts.text: An elder keeps what a village would rather forget: who owns which field, who owes what, and what happened the last time.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › counts everything twice

facts.text: Nobody learns a craft by being told. You show it once, watch it done badly, and say less than you want to.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Some learn by watching

facts.text: A tinker fixes with what's to hand: a split pin, a twist of wire, a buckle somebody else threw away.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › You can fix nearly anything with what other people throw away

facts.text: Copper is the soft metal: it works cold, it goes green in the rain, and it comes out of the northern mountains beside the iron.
facts.source: WORLD.md § Resource geography › Iron, copper, mana-granite

facts.text: Split timber along the grain, never across it, and season it a year before it goes into anything that has to last.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › techniques: ['grain', 'notching', 'seasoning']

facts.text: Every stone has a bed. Split along it, lay it the way it lay in the ground, and a dry-stone wall stands on weight and fit alone.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › techniques: ['cleave', 'knapping', 'drystone']

facts.text: Dress a kill the day it falls. A hide left overnight starts to slip its hair, and then it's only good for glue.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › techniques: ['sign', 'stalking', 'dressing']

facts.text: Hide makes the warmest clothes on the road: a parka sewn fur-in, the seams doubled and greased against the wet.
facts.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › 'hide-parka', 'waterskin'
